newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends down as record run hits buffers.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends down as record run hits buffers.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 closes lower for first time in 12 sessions.
** Strong Dow lends support after sharp 0.6 percent drop in
U.S. producer prices for April, but UK index unable to
extend record-breaking run of past eight sessions.
** Safeway gains 7pct after results show rising sales.

Ian Scott, strategist at U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers, said Labour's budget -- which could set out to remove some of the tax priviliges for pension funds in owning UK shares -- was the only real cloud on the horizon for UK markets.

"A period of consolidation is probably warranted," Scott said. "But beyond a short-term trading view, it's difficult to see what could undermine the market, apart from a big surprise in the budget...and it would have to be a pretty drastic surprise to really undermine things."

Pointing to Lehman's recent increase in its year-end target for the FTSE 100 to 5,000, Scott said the market should rise yet further through the rest of the year, with no sign that inflation was likely to pick up in the UK or the United States.
"Clearly we do think the market can go higher," he said.

Profit-taking sent the UK market lower during the morning session, with the market also unsettled by comments from the Bank of England on Tuesday that UK interest rates would have to rise further to ward off inflationary pressures.

Yet the market rebounded by the close as Wall Street opened higher on the back of a sharp 0.6 percent drop in April producer prices, which eased the market's concerns about the threat of rising U.S. interest rates.
The Dow was up about 52 points as the London equity market closed.
By contrast, UK jobless figures showing March underlying average earnings up a lower-than-expected 4.5 percent had little lasting impact on share prices or gilts.
The long gilt future was up 5/16 shortly after the stock market close, tracking gains in U.S. Treasury bonds, where the benchmark 30-year issue was also up 5/16, cutting its yield to 6.87 percent.

Trading volume reached an active 823 million shares by 1633 GMT. The FTSE 250 index of mid-range shares fell 3.7 points to 4,529.3 while the Reuters-HSBC index of the top 150 shares fell 1.22 points to 1,250.98.

Dealers said many UK institutional investors, awash with cash and convinced the FTSE's medium-term trend is still upwards, have been reluctant to sell stock, leaving market makers scrambling to fill large orders -- and producing sharp gains in some leading stocks.

The market was also underpinned by continuing hopes that further deals similar to the merger between Grand Metropolitan and Guinness Plc would surface soon. "You can almost smell another merger or a takeover bid out there," another senior dealer said.
Yet others said such "squeezy" market conditions made recent moves a poor guide to the underlying trend.
"We have seen another good performance today but the market is still nervous," said a senior sales trader at one top brokerage.
"Every time we go to another record, people get twitchy, they are nervous if they are not in the market and nervous if they are, because there could be a major correction at some stage."

British Airways was among stocks squeezed higher by relatively small buying interest, up 18p at 12.93-1/2 after earlier reaching a record 12.97 stg. BA was given a further boost as Lufthansa detailed its airline alliance with United Airlines, renewing hopes for BA's planned linkup with American Airlines.

Supermarket operator Safeway was the day's biggest gainer in the FTSE 100, up 23p or 6.9 percent at 354 after results enlivened by a 3.7 percent rise in same-store sales in the first six weeks of the current year.
Yet the news helped knock second-tier supermarket group Kwik Save, down 13-1/2p at 267 on fears it was losing market share.

P&O was up 14-1/2p at 635-1/2 after a recommendation earlier this week from SBC Warburg, while Cable & Wireless slipped 12p to 500-1/2 after the company reported full-year pre-tax profits of 1.42 billion stg, no better than the market expected.
Vodafone, down 6p to 275-1/2 and Orange Plc off 7 at 216-1/2, lost ground on worries about a possible new mobile phone levy that could be introduced by the new Labour government.

Insurance stocks were also mostly lower, with General Accident down 12p at 945-1/2 despite first-quarter results showing doubled operating profits, as UBS repeated a "sell" on the stock, while Commercial Union fell 15p to 734-1/2 after first-quarter results in line with expectations.

Reckitt & Colman gained 17-1/2p to 906-1/2 after an upbeat statement at its annual shareholders meeting and as NatWest raised the stock to "buy" from "hold" while Ladbroke lost 8p to 246-1/2 as James Capel cut the stock to "hold" from "buy."
Outside the FTSE 100, Datrontech plummeted 49-1/2p to 160 on a profit warning.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
